east-fairview-mennonite-milford-ne.assessment: East Fairview Mennonite Church traces its roots to the 1870s migration of Amish Mennonite families from Ohio and Illinois to Nebraska. Formally organized in spring 1876 with 23 members and first pastor P. P. Hershberger, the congregation has continuously served the Milford area for 150 years and now reports 173 members. Pastor Kyle Roth currently leads. The deep generational continuity, strong CMC/Rosedale conservative Anabaptist accountability, and significant membership size make East Fairview a flagship Nebraska Mennonite congregation. Green rating reflects strong confessional, gender, and leadership integrity.

east-whittier-friends-church-ca.assessment: East Whittier Friends Church is the lifelong home meeting of Richard Milhous Nixon — the 37th President was raised here from age 9, played piano in Sunday school, taught Sunday school as a young attorney, and remained a member until his death in 1994. The congregation is part of Friends Southwest, the evangelical/programmed branch of Quakerism — distinct from the liberal unprogrammed Friends General Conference (FGC) and Friends United Meeting (FUM) which have moved toward LGBT affirmation. Evangelical Friends affirm Trinitarian orthodoxy, biblical authority, and grace-through-faith soteriology in the Richmond Declaration tradition. Worship is bilingual (English/Spanish) and programmed — looking more like a contemporary evangelical service than the silent meetings stereotypically associated with Quakers. Female pastoral leadership is present (Pastora Delia Madrid) — consistent with Quakerism's 17th-century affirmation of women in ministry, but yellow on MOOP's rubric. Solid green at the denominational and theological core; historic Americana.

eastside-baptist-twin-falls-id.assessment: Eastside Baptist Church in Twin Falls, Idaho is a 1689 Confessional Reformed Baptist church with a plurality of elders, age-integrated worship, and a robust confessional foundation. Founded in 1972, this church holds to the full 1689 London Baptist Confession including the appendix on baptism. The elder-led structure (Thompson, Martinez) with deacons reflects biblical governance. Their adoption of resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription demonstrates a church willing to take stands on cultural issues from Scripture — not hiding behind neutrality. Men's Book Study and age-integrated model mean men are formed as household leaders, not shuffled into a separate program. Four services per week (Sunday AM, Sunday PM, Sunday School, Wednesday evening) indicates a serious, committed congregation. This is an all-GREEN church — rare and worthy of attention for any Reformed Baptist in the Pacific Northwest.

score_notes.gender: Age-integrated worship, elder-led by men only. Adopted resolution on women's conscription — explicitly patriarchal position. GREEN — not merely complementarian.
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of elders (Paul Thompson, John Martinez) with deacons (Dan Steineke, Scott Pierce). Biblical elder governance under 1689 Confession.
